title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This chart records three years of cardio-renal-metabolic care for PAT-001. It documents (a) the chronic management of type 2 diabetes (DIS-001), hypertension (DIS-002), chronic kidney disease (DIS-003), and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (DIS-004); (b) the hyperkalemia admission of 2025-09-17 to 2025-09-20 (DIS-019, INC-002); and (c) the metformin renal-dose adjustment of 2025-03-13 under PRO-008. Policy values are cited, not defined, here; the authoritative text for each policy is in the HO documents named above.

text: ## 8. Visit Narratives

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 8.1 ENC-001-01, 2024-01-18 (baseline visit) Mr. Doyle attended for scheduled review. He reported stable exertional dyspnea at two flights of stairs and no orthopnea. Examination: BP 148/86, heart rate 74 regular, mild ankle edema, lungs clear. Laboratory results (LD-03): HbA1c 8.1%, creatinine 142 umol/L (eGFR 49 mL/min/1.73 m2, stage G3a at that time), potassium 4.7 mmol/L. Plan: refer to cardiology for echocardiography; continue metformin 1,000 mg twice daily (eGFR at that date was above the PRO-008 cap threshold of 45); repeat labs in 6 months.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 8.2 ENC-001-02 and ENC-001-03, cardiology (2024-02-12, 2024-06-04) The echocardiogram (LAB-023, report in LD-06) showed LVEF 34%, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter 6.1 cm, and mild functional mitral regurgitation. The 12-lead ECG (LAB-021) showed sinus rhythm at 76 beats per minute with a QRS duration of 108 ms. Dr. Rohan Deshmukh-Ellis (STF-005) started metoprolol succinate 50 mg, increased to 100 mg on 2024-06-04, and started spironolactone 25 mg on the same day, with a safety potassium and creatinine check booked at one week (ENC-001-04: K 4.9, eGFR 48). The guideline reference for these steps is DG-01.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 8.3 ENC-001-06, 2024-11-05 NT-proBNP (LAB-008) fell from 1,850 to 1,120 pg/mL. Blood pressure remained above target at 142/84, so lisinopril was increased from 10 mg to 20 mg daily. Potassium 4.8 mmol/L was noted as acceptable but at the upper end of the clinic comfort range; a recheck at the next visit was requested. The potential for hyperkalemia with MED-004 plus MED-008 is described in MP-06 and MP-01.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
section: 8.4 ENC-001-07 to ENC-001-09, the metformin adjustment (2025-02-20 to 2025-05-14)
text: ### 8.4 ENC-001-07 to ENC-001-09, the metformin adjustment (2025-02-20 to 2025-05-14) On 2025-02-20 creatinine was 158 umol/L, eGFR 44. Under PRO-008 (see HO-02), metformin is capped at 1,000 mg/day when eGFR is 30 to 44 (FPA-03). The PharmaSafe system generated a renal-dose advisory, but it was filed in the pharmacist work queue rather than the prescriber inbox. The dose therefore remained 2,000 mg/day for **21 days** until the pharmacist telephone review of 2025-03-13 (ENC-001-08), when the dose was reduced to 500 mg twice daily and the patient was counseled on sick-day rules. At ENC-001-09 (2025-05-14), eGFR 43 with metformin 1,000 mg/day was compliant. Metformin would be stopped if eGFR fell below 30; it has not.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 8.5 ENC-001-11 and ENC-001-12, post-admission titration After the hyperkalemia admission (section 9), the heart failure clinic restarted lisinopril cautiously at 5 mg (2025-09-26). On 2025-10-23 a joint cardiology and nephrology review (STF-005, STF-007) increased lisinopril to 10 mg and resumed spironolactone at half the previous dose (12.5 mg), with potassium checks at 1 and 4 weeks. The 4-week check on 2025-11-20 gave K 4.8 mmol/L. The renal rationale is in DG-03.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 8.6 ENC-001-14 and ENC-001-15, 2026 follow-up On 2026-04-08 HbA1c was 7.1%, NT-proBNP 940 pg/mL, creatinine 170 umol/L (eGFR 39). On 2026-09-02 the repeat echocardiogram (LAB-023) showed LVEF 38%; the ECG (LAB-021) showed sinus rhythm at 68 beats per minute, QRS 108 ms. HbA1c 7.0%, K 4.7, creatinine 168 umol/L (eGFR 40). Allergy status re-verified as none. No medication changes were made. The next review is booked for 2027-03.

text: ## 9. Hyperkalemia Admission, 2025-09-17 to 2025-09-20 (ENC-001-10, INC-002)

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-001 (Marcus E. Doyle)
text: ### 9.1 Background For three days before presentation, Mr. Doyle had vomiting and diarrhea with poor oral intake. He continued lisinopril 20 mg, spironolactone 25 mg, furosemide 40 mg, and metformin. He presented to the Emergency Department (DEP-001) on 2025-09-17 with generalized weakness and palpitations.

text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This chart follows PAT-002 through three connected events: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (DIS-005) managed with an anticoagulant, a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (DIS-006) on 2025-03-03 treated with a coronary stent and combined antithrombotic therapy, and an upper gastrointestinal bleed (DIS-022) on 2025-05-19 with resulting iron-deficiency anemia (DIS-018). The central questions answered by this record are which antithrombotic agents were used when, why aspirin was stopped at discharge, and how bleeding was managed without abandoning stent protection.

text: ### 7.2 Procedure and echo Coronary angiography on 2025-03-04 at 10:30 (DEP-003) showed a 90% mid-left-anterior-descending stenosis treated with one drug-eluting stent. Clopidogrel 300 mg was loaded before the procedure. Echocardiogram on 2025-03-04 (LAB-023, LD-06): LVEF 50% with mild apical hypokinesis.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-002 (Priya Nandakumar)
text: ### 7.3 Antithrombotic decision and recorded rationale Apixaban was resumed on 2025-03-05 at 08:00. The pharmacist-verification requirement for apixaban orders (FPA-04, 4 hours) was met: order entered 08:00, verified 09:12 (72 minutes). From 2025-03-05 to 2025-03-07 the patient therefore took three agents (apixaban, clopidogrel, aspirin 81 mg). At discharge on 2025-03-07 the cardiology team **stopped aspirin and continued apixaban 5 mg twice daily with clopidogrel 75 mg daily**. The recorded rationale was: (1) DG-01 limits aspirin in patients with atrial fibrillation who need an anticoagulant to a peri-procedural course of no more than 7 days; aspirin had been given for 5 days; (2) the bleeding-risk score on the DG-01 rubric was 3 (age over 65, low body weight, hypertension), indicating elevated risk; (3) PRO-007 (HO-04) requires pharmacist review of any combination containing an anticoagulant and an antiplatelet, which was completed on 2025-03-06. The apixaban dose-reduction criteria in MP-03 were reviewed: only one of the three criteria was present (weight 58 kg; age under 80; creatinine 0.9 mg/dL with eGFR 72), so the full dose was kept. Clopidogrel was planned for six months to 2025-09-04.

text: ### 6.5 Hospital-onset C. difficile infection (INC-004) Watery diarrhea began on the evening of 2026-03-06 (hospital day 9). A stool specimen for C. difficile toxin/PCR (LAB-024) was sent at 22:10. The positive result was verified at **08:40 on 2026-03-07**. Contact-enteric precautions (PRO-012) were not started until **15:25**, an interval of 6 hours 45 minutes. During this interval the patient used a shared bathroom with one other patient (no secondary case identified on screening). The delay was reported as **INC-004** and reviewed in HO-08. Treatment: oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours (MED-019, oral route) from 2026-03-07 for 10 days, last dose 2026-03-16. Diarrhea resolved at 06:00 on 2026-03-12. Under FPA-10 precautions continue until 72 hours after diarrhea resolves, so they ended at 06:00 on 2026-03-15 (HO-06). Discharge occurred on 2026-03-16 at 10:20.

text: ## 7. Admission for Ketoacidosis, 2025-12-09 to 2025-12-12 (ENC-004-03)

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-004 (Elena Voss)
text: ### 7.1 Background Three days of fever (38.4 C), vomiting, and almost no oral intake after a household viral illness. The patient continued empagliflozin and metformin and reduced insulin glargine to 10 units. She presented to DEP-001 at 19:10 on 2025-12-09 with abdominal pain, rapid breathing, and drowsiness.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-004 (Elena Voss)
text: ### 7.2 Initial results | Test | Result | |---|---| | Glucose (LAB-028) | 11.8 mmol/L (212 mg/dL), only mildly raised | | Beta-hydroxybutyrate (LAB-028), 20:00 | 5.4 mmol/L | | ABG (LAB-018) | pH 7.18, bicarbonate 9 mmol/L, PaCO2 2.4 kPa (18 mmHg) | | BMP (LAB-002) | Sodium 137, potassium 3.3 mmol/L (LAB-005), creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, eGFR 88, anion gap 24 | | HbA1c (LAB-003) | 7.6% | | TSH (LAB-017), drawn 2025-12-10 | 4.1 mIU/L | Because the glucose was not markedly elevated, the diagnosis rested on ketones and acidosis, in line with DG-02. The pattern was attributed to empagliflozin combined with starvation and reduced insulin.

section: 7.3 Insulin infusion and ketone series (PRO-010, FPA-12)
text: ### 7.3 Insulin infusion and ketone series (PRO-010, FPA-12) An insulin regular infusion (MED-003) was begun at 19:55 at 0.1 units per kg per hour (7.2 units/h) with fluids and potassium replacement (a non-registry electrolyte agent). Admission to DEP-009 for monitoring. | Time | Beta-hydroxybutyrate (mmol/L) | Comment | |---|---|---| | 2025-12-09 20:00 | 5.4 | Baseline | | 21:00 | 4.8 | | | 23:00 | 3.9 | | | 2025-12-10 02:00 | 2.6 | | | 06:00 | 1.5 | K 3.9 mmol/L | | 10:00 | 0.9 | | | 14:00 | 0.5 | First value below 0.6 | | 16:00 | 0.4 | Second consecutive value below 0.6 | **Transition criterion:** FPA-12 requires beta-hydroxybutyrate below 0.6 mmol/L on two consecutive checks. The criterion was first met at **16:00 on 2025-12-10**. Insulin glargine 20 units was given subcutaneously at 16:30 and the infusion was stopped at 18:30 after a two-hour overlap.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-004 (Elena Voss)
text: ### 7.4 Hypoglycemia alert At 03:20 on 2025-12-10 the capillary glucose was 3.8 mmol/L (68 mg/dL). The hypoglycemia alert threshold in FPA-12 is below 4.0 mmol/L, so the alert was triggered. Dextrose 10% was added to the infusion fluid and the glucose rose to 6.2 mmol/L by 04:20. Ketone clearance continued.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-004 (Elena Voss)
text: ### 7.5 Discharge and decisions Metformin was resumed 2025-12-12 once oral intake was normal. Empagliflozin was permanently discontinued and entered as an adverse drug reaction; MP-02 and DG-02 describe the contraindication for re-challenge. Discharged 2025-12-12 on glargine 20 units, metformin 1,000 mg twice daily, levothyroxine 88 micrograms. Patient re-taught sick-day rules by diabetes educator.

text: ### 7.3 Antiplatelet choice Aspirin is the standard first antiplatelet in DG-06, but it is contraindicated for PAT-005 because of ALG-003. Clopidogrel was chosen as the documented alternative (DG-06, MP-03, MP-07).

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-005 (Samuel Adeyemi-Clarke)
text: ### 7.4 Anticoagulation timing and verification DG-06 states that after a moderate stroke (NIHSS 5 to 15 at presentation) in a patient with atrial fibrillation, an anticoagulant is started between day 4 and day 7 if repeat imaging shows no hemorrhagic transformation. Day 0 was 2026-04-14. Imaging on day 4 was clear, so apixaban was ordered at 08:30 on 2026-04-19 (day 5) and clopidogrel was stopped (last dose 2026-04-18). The dose-reduction criteria in MP-03 were reviewed: age 76, weight 81 kg, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL; none of the three criteria was met, so 5 mg twice daily was used. FPA-04 requires pharmacist verification of new apixaban orders within 4 hours; verification was at 10:05, 95 minutes after the order: **met**.

text: ### 7.5 Other management Blood pressure was permitted to run higher for 48 hours, then amlodipine was raised to 10 mg on 2026-04-20. Albuterol was continued. Speech and physical therapy began on day 2. Discharged home on 2026-04-22 with outpatient rehabilitation.

title: Longitudinal Chart: PAT-006 (Grace Lindqvist-Obi)
text: ### 8.2 Management Ciprofloxacin was stopped after 5 days. Stewardship (DEP-007, PRO-013) reviewed the course and accepted 5 days because symptoms had resolved and the interaction harm outweighed further benefit; a repeat urine culture on 2025-11-04 was negative. Warfarin was held on 2025-10-26 and 2025-10-27. INR was 4.1 on 2025-10-27, 3.2 on 2025-10-28, and 2.6 on 2025-10-29. Warfarin resumed on 2025-10-28 at 4 mg daily. Hemoglobin on 2025-10-26 was 12.9 g/dL; there was no major bleeding. The anticoagulation rule that an INR above 4.5 triggers a clinic call within 24 hours (FPA-05) was **met**. The overridden alert, with no INR plan, was reported as **INC-003** and reviewed in HO-08. Warfarin was completed on 2025-11-29 (about 3 months from 2025-08-29).

text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This casebook holds four patients selected for distinct medication-safety lessons: a penicillin anaphylaxis incident (PAT-007, INC-001), an acute coronary syndrome in a man who cannot take ACE inhibitors (PAT-008), acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease after an NSAID prescription (PAT-009, INC-005), and a gastrointestinal bleed on an SSRI combined with two antiplatelet-acting drugs (PAT-010). Each patient has an independent allergy and medication profile; do not combine facts between sections. Laboratory values for these patients are given inline unless a separate report is cited.

text: ### 3.3 Outcome and follow-up The patient stayed 24 hours in the ICU, then on a ward. She was discharged on 2026-05-19 with an epinephrine auto-injector prescription (MED-029) and a revised allergy entry: **ALG-001, anaphylaxis, confirmed 2026-05-17**; cephalosporin cross-reactivity cautions were added per MP-07. Allergy clinic referral was made. Spirometry (LAB-019) on 2026-06-23 (LD-08): FEV1 82% of predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.78, bronchodilator reversibility 14%, supporting well-controlled asthma. The event was reported as **INC-001**; the review, the change to PRO-003 (a hard stop on override of the dual-verification step for beta-lactams, effective 2026-07-01), and the audit findings are in HO-08. Contrast this case with PAT-012 in PR-08, who tolerated the same antibiotic and has no allergy flag.

text: ### 4.2 Management Coronary angiography on 2026-02-04 (DEP-003) showed a 85% right coronary artery stenosis treated with one drug-eluting stent. Echocardiogram (LAB-023, LD-06): LVEF 48%, mild inferior hypokinesis. Metoprolol succinate was started at 25 mg and raised to 50 mg daily; atorvastatin 80 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily long term; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months.

title: Admission Casebook A: PAT-007, PAT-008, PAT-009, PAT-010
text: ### 4.3 The ACE-inhibitor decision DG-01 recommends a renin-angiotensin system blocker after ACS when LVEF is below 50% or hypertension persists. For PAT-008 the standard choice, an ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril (MED-004), is **contraindicated by ALG-004** (MP-01, MP-06, MP-07). MP-01 also advises caution with related receptor-blocking agents after ACE-inhibitor angioedema. No renin-angiotensin agent was started; blood pressure was addressed with metoprolol and cardiology re-review planned at 6 weeks (completed 2026-03-17, BP 132/80). Discharged 2026-02-07. Compare PAT-001 (PR-01), who takes lisinopril without any allergy flag.

text: ### 5.1 Background and the prescription (INC-005) Baseline creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (115 umol/L), eGFR 40, on 2026-03-05. text: ### 6.1 Medication reconciliation finding (PRO-001) On admission the pharmacist interview found aspirin 81 mg taken daily, bought over the counter for "heart prevention," which was not on the medication list. Ibuprofen had been prescribed 2026-04-14 for hand and knee osteoarthritis. Upper endoscopy on 2026-06-11: 1.5 cm gastric antral ulcer with a clean base; no endoscopic therapy; H. pylori stool antigen negative. No transfusion was required. Pantoprazole 40 mg IV twice daily then 40 mg orally twice daily for 8 weeks (MED-028). Ibuprofen and aspirin were stopped permanently; acetaminophen (MED-027) was used for arthritis pain. Sertraline was **continued** because depression was stable, with the PPI as protection (DG-08 conflict rule). Hb 9.6 g/dL at discharge on 2026-06-14 and 12.8 g/dL on 2026-07-22. **Differences from PAT-002 (PR-02), a similar bleed:** PAT-010 had a gastric ulcer, a 5.8 g/dL fall from baseline, no transfusion, and no anticoagulant; PAT-002 had a duodenal ulcer with a visible vessel, two units transfused, and was on apixaban and clopidogrel.

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This casebook holds four patients: a heart-failure readmission with a missed follow-up call in a man on warfarin (PAT-011, INC-006), a non-severe pneumonia treated with a short, stewardship-guided course (PAT-012), urosepsis with acute kidney injury and pharmacy-managed vancomycin (PAT-013), and iron-deficiency anemia complicated by a levothyroxine absorption problem (PAT-014). Facts are specific to each patient; several features deliberately resemble charts in PR-01, PR-03, PR-06 and PR-07 and must not be confused with them. Laboratory values are given inline unless a separate report is cited.

text: ### 3.1 First admission, 2026-01-12 to 2026-01-17 (ENC-011-01) Admitted with three weeks of worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and edema; weight 79.8 kg. NT-proBNP (LAB-008) 4,820 pg/mL. ECG (LAB-021): atrial fibrillation, rate 96. Echocardiogram (LAB-023, LD-06) on 2026-01-13: LVEF 30%. INR (LAB-010) 2.6. Potassium 4.5 mmol/L, eGFR 52. Intravenous furosemide produced a 3.8 kg loss; at discharge furosemide was increased from 40 mg daily to 40 mg twice daily. Discharged **2026-01-17 at 14:30**.

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 3.3 What happened (INC-006) - The discharge contact number had two digits transposed. The single call attempt on 2026-01-19 at 11:05 reached a wrong number; no second attempt was made and no escalation to the emergency contact occurred. - The clinic appointment for 2026-01-23 was missed (no-show) and no outreach followed. - No INR check took place within 72 hours. The HF follow-up calls (DEP-014, with clinical co-ownership by DEP-003) therefore **did not meet** FPA-06. Review of the incident is in HO-08.

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 3.4 Readmission, 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-08 (ENC-011-02) Returned 16 days after discharge with dyspnea and weight 80.1 kg (4.1 kg above dry weight). NT-proBNP 5,300 pg/mL. INR **3.4**, above the 2.0 to 3.0 target. Warfarin was reduced from 4 mg to 3.5 mg daily and an INR recheck was set for 2026-02-05 (3 days), when INR was 2.8. Diuresis resumed; furosemide 40 mg twice daily continued; spironolactone continued (K 4.6). The patient reported a high-salt diet and missing two metoprolol doses per week. Discharged **2026-02-08 at 11:00** with all three obligations met: call completed 2026-02-09 at 09:30 (22 hours 30 minutes), INR 2.6 on 2026-02-10, clinic visit 2026-02-12 (4 days). The case is the principal example of a missed heart-failure follow-up in this dataset; PAT-001 (PR-01) in contrast completed all follow-up on time.

Chest X-ray (LAB-020): right middle lobe infiltrate. Procalcitonin (LAB-015) **0.42 ng/mL**; C-reactive protein (LAB-016) 96 mg/L; eGFR 82; HbA1c 7.4%. Because PAT-012 has **no allergy flag**, the dual-verification rule (FPA-09) did not apply; the first dose of amoxicillin-clavulanate was given at 13:20 on 2026-05-05 after standard verification. title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 4.2 Course and stewardship decision Afebrile since 06:00 on 2026-05-06. Procalcitonin on 2026-05-07 was **0.18 ng/mL**. Under DG-05 a non-severe pneumonia in a clinically stable patient is treated for a minimum of 5 days; under the stewardship rule in HO-04 (PRO-013), antibiotics may stop at day 5 when procalcitonin is below 0.25 ng/mL and the patient has been afebrile for at least 48 hours. Both conditions were met, and antibiotics were stopped after the final dose on **2026-05-09 (day 5)**. Metformin was continued (eGFR above the FPA-03 renal band). Discharged 2026-05-08. Follow-up chest X-ray on 2026-06-19 was clear.

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 6.1 Diagnosis, 2026-03-30 Fatigue for four months. Hemoglobin (LAB-001) **9.8 g/dL**, MCV 71 fL; ferritin (LAB-025) **7 ng/mL**; TSH (LAB-017) 2.4 mIU/L. DG-07 defines iron-deficiency anemia in women as hemoglobin below 12.0 g/dL with ferritin below 15 ng/mL; both criteria were met. Upper endoscopy and colonoscopy on 2026-04-20 showed mild gastritis and no bleeding source. Heavy perimenopausal menstrual bleeding was identified as the likely source and managed by gynecology (a non-registry service).

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 6.2 The levothyroxine problem Ferrous sulfate was started 2026-04-07, taken at 07:00, 30 minutes after levothyroxine at 06:30. On 2026-05-12 TSH was **8.9 mIU/L** although the levothyroxine dose had not changed. The cause was reduced levothyroxine absorption from co-administered iron (MP-06, MP-02). Under FPA-14 the two must be separated by at least 4 hours. The schedule was changed to **levothyroxine at 06:30 and ferrous sulfate at 14:00** (7.5 hours apart). TSH on 2026-07-14 was 3.2 mIU/L, with no change in levothyroxine dose.

title: Admission Casebook B: PAT-011, PAT-012, PAT-013, PAT-014
text: ### 6.3 Response On 2026-07-14: hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, ferritin 38 ng/mL. On 2026-09-18: hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, ferritin 61 ng/mL, TSH 3.0. Iron continues until 2026-10-14 (three months after hemoglobin normalized).

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline defines how MediCore diagnoses and treats four cardiovascular conditions. It supplies the criteria that patient charts (PR-01, PR-02, PR-05, PR-07, PR-08) apply and that protocols (HO-03, HO-07) implement with MediCore time targets. Where a time target appears here it is labeled as a pointer to the protocol; the authoritative value is in the HO document.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Hypertension (DIS-002)

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Diagnosis and targets Hypertension is diagnosed when clinic blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg or higher on two visits, or 135/85 mmHg or higher on home monitoring. The treatment target is below 140/90 mmHg for most adults and **below 130/80 mmHg** for patients with diabetes (DIS-001), chronic kidney disease (DIS-003), or established cardiovascular disease.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Drug selection | Situation | Preferred agent | Notes | |---|---|---| | Hypertension with HFrEF, diabetes, or CKD | ACE inhibitor: lisinopril (MED-004) | Check potassium and creatinine at baseline, 1 week, and after each dose increase | | Hypertension without compelling indication | Calcium-channel blocker: amlodipine (MED-005) | Ankle edema is the commonest adverse effect | | Hypertension after myocardial infarction | Beta-blocker: metoprolol succinate (MED-006) | Cardioselective; see asthma caution in DG-04 | | Hypertension with fluid overload | Loop diuretic: furosemide (MED-007) | Monitor potassium and renal function |

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 3.3 When an ACE inhibitor must not be used
text: ### 3.3 When an ACE inhibitor must not be used An ACE inhibitor is **contraindicated** after a previous episode of ACE-inhibitor-associated angioedema (ALG-004). Related receptor-blocking agents also require caution because angioedema can recur at a lower rate (MP-01, MP-06, MP-07). Example: PAT-008 (PR-07).

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 4. Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (DIS-004)
text: ## 4. Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (DIS-004)

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Diagnosis HFrEF requires symptoms or signs of heart failure plus a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of **40% or lower** on echocardiography (LAB-023). NT-proBNP (LAB-008) supports the diagnosis when above 450 pg/mL under age 50, above 900 pg/mL between 50 and 75, and above 1,800 pg/mL over 75. NT-proBNP is not a stand-alone diagnostic test.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Treatment pillars | Pillar | Agent | Reference rule | |---|---|---| | Renin-angiotensin blockade | Lisinopril (MED-004) | Titrate to tolerated dose; hold during vomiting, diarrhea, or hyperkalemia | | Beta-blocker | Metoprolol succinate (MED-006) | Start low; double at 2-week intervals if heart rate and blood pressure allow | | Mineralocorticoid antagonist | Spironolactone (MED-008) | Start when potassium is 5.0 mmol/L or lower and eGFR is 30 or higher | | Congestion control | Furosemide (MED-007) | Lowest dose that maintains dry weight |

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Potassium safety for mineralocorticoid antagonists Check potassium (LAB-005) and creatinine/eGFR (LAB-004) at **1 week and 4 weeks** after starting or increasing spironolactone. Do not increase the dose when potassium is above 5.0 mmol/L. Hold spironolactone and the ACE inhibitor if potassium reaches 5.5 mmol/L or higher; the management algorithm is in DG-03. The combination of MED-004 with MED-008 in CKD is a recognized hyperkalemia hazard (MP-06, MP-01); PAT-001 (PR-01) illustrates the monitoring schedule.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Sick-day rule During vomiting, diarrhea, or poor oral intake the patient should pause the ACE inhibitor, spironolactone, diuretic, and metformin until eating and drinking normally for 24 to 48 hours.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.5 After discharge Discharge after a heart-failure admission requires structured follow-up. The MediCore protocol is PRO-016 in HO-07, which sets a telephone call within 48 hours and a clinic visit within 7 days (FPA-06). Patients on warfarin (MED-013) also need an INR check within 72 hours of discharge under PRO-007 (HO-04). PAT-011 (PR-08) shows what happens when these steps fail.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Atrial Fibrillation (DIS-005)

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Diagnosis Diagnose by 12-lead ECG (LAB-021) or a monitor strip showing at least 30 seconds of irregular rhythm without discernible P waves. Paroxysmal AF terminates within 7 days; persistent AF lasts longer. Echocardiography (LAB-023) is indicated at diagnosis.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Stroke prevention An oral anticoagulant is recommended in adults with AF at moderate or high stroke risk. First choice is apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MED-012); warfarin (MED-013, target INR 2.0 to 3.0) is used when apixaban is unsuitable. Dose-reduction criteria for apixaban are in MP-03.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.3 Bleeding-risk rubric (MediCore Bleeding-Risk Rubric, fictional) One point each for: age over 65; body weight under 60 kg; hypertension; previous major bleed; renal impairment (eGFR below 45); concomitant antiplatelet drug. A score of **3 or more** is elevated risk and prompts minimization of concomitant antiplatelet therapy and use of a proton pump inhibitor (MED-028). PAT-002 (PR-02) scored 3.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.4 Rate control Metoprolol succinate (MED-006) is the first-line rate-control agent when LVEF is reduced or after myocardial infarction.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 6. Acute Coronary Syndrome (DIS-006)

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.1 Diagnosis ACS is diagnosed from symptoms, ECG (LAB-021), and hs-troponin (LAB-007). Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) requires a rise and/or fall of hs-troponin above the 99th percentile in the LD-01 range with ischemic symptoms or ECG change. Serial sampling at 0 and 2 hours is the MediCore standard (FPA-08; HO-03). ST-depression, as in PAT-002 and PAT-008, supports the diagnosis but is not required.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.2 Initial treatment Aspirin 300 mg loading dose (MED-010) unless contraindicated; clopidogrel 300 mg loading dose (MED-011) before angiography; high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg, MED-009); beta-blocker (MED-006) if no contraindication. If aspirin is contraindicated (ALG-003), clopidogrel alone is used for the antiplatelet effect (MP-07).

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 6.3 Antithrombotic therapy when ACS and AF coexist
text: ### 6.3 Antithrombotic therapy when ACS and AF coexist This situation requires balancing stent thrombosis against bleeding. | Rule | Reference guideline statement | |---|---| | Aspirin duration | Aspirin is added only for the peri-procedural period and is limited to **7 days or less** | | Anticoagulant | Continue or resume apixaban (MED-012) as soon as the procedure is complete | | P2Y12 inhibitor | Clopidogrel 75 mg daily for **6 months** after the stent, together with apixaban; then apixaban alone | | Gastric protection | Proton pump inhibitor for the duration of combined therapy | | Review | Pharmacist review of every combination with an anticoagulant and an antiplatelet (PRO-007, HO-04) | PAT-002 (PR-02) followed this pattern: aspirin for 5 days, clopidogrel to 2025-09-04.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.4 ACS without AF Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg) continues for **12 months**. PAT-008 (PR-07) follows this schedule.

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.5 Renin-angiotensin blockade after ACS An ACE inhibitor is recommended after ACS when LVEF is below 50% or hypertension persists. If an ACE inhibitor is contraindicated (ALG-004), no alternative agent is started automatically; cardiology reviews at 6 weeks (MP-01).

title: Cardiovascular Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.6 Pathway timing Time-critical steps (ECG within 10 minutes of arrival; 0 and 2 hour hs-troponin; critical-result calling) are MediCore protocols owned by PRO-006 and PRO-009 in HO-03 and HO-05.

section: DG-02: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: # DG-02: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference) > **SYNTHETIC DATA NOTICE.** This document is a fictional reference guideline written for software benchmarking and education. Its criteria, thresholds, and algorithms are invented, may differ from real-world practice, and must not be used for clinical decisions. "Reference Guideline" statements are kept separate from "MediCore Policy" statements owned by the HO documents.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 1. Document Control | Field | Value | |---|---| | Document ID | DG-02 | | Folder | 02_Diseases_Clinical_Guidelines | | Version / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-01 | | Conditions covered | Type 2 diabetes (DIS-001), diabetic ketoacidosis (DIS-013), hyperlipidemia (DIS-014), hypothyroidism (DIS-016) | | Owner | Endocrinology and Diabetes (DEP-004, head STF-006), approved by the CPRB | | Companion documents | MP-02, MP-06, MP-07, LD-01, LD-03, LD-04, HO-02 |

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline gives diagnostic criteria, targets, and treatment rules for four endocrine and metabolic conditions. It is the clinical rationale behind the renal dose cap for metformin (operationalized in PRO-008), the SGLT2-inhibitor safety rules, the insulin-infusion transition (operationalized in PRO-010), and the levothyroxine separation rule. Charts that apply it are PR-01, PR-04, PR-07 and PR-08.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (DIS-001)

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Diagnosis Diagnose with HbA1c (LAB-003) of **6.5% or higher** or fasting glucose of 7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) or higher, confirmed on a second occasion unless symptomatic with a random glucose of 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) or higher.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Targets HbA1c target is **7.0% to 7.5%** for most adults. Less stringent targets (up to 8.0%) are acceptable in frail patients or those with limited life expectancy. Blood pressure target is below 130/80 mmHg (DG-01); lipid targets are in section 5.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Treatment | Step | Agent | Rule | |---|---|---| | First line | Metformin (MED-001) | Start 500 mg daily; titrate to 1,000 mg twice daily if eGFR allows | | Add-on | SGLT2 inhibitor: empagliflozin (MED-030) | Only with sick-day teaching; see 3.5 | | Insulin | Basal insulin glargine (MED-002) | Start 10 units nightly or 0.1 to 0.2 units/kg; titrate to fasting glucose |

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 3.4 Metformin and kidney function (rationale for the renal cap)
text: ### 3.4 Metformin and kidney function (rationale for the renal cap) Metformin is renally cleared; accumulation raises the risk of lactic acidosis. The reference guideline rule is: | eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) | Rule | |---|---| | 45 or higher | No reduction required | | **30 to 44** | **Maximum 1,000 mg per day** | | Below 30 | Stop | MediCore applies this rule through PRO-008 and FPA-03 (HO-02); the practical dose tables are in MP-02 and MP-07. During acute illness with dehydration, pause metformin (sick-day rule). Charts showing the rule in action: PR-01 (eGFR 44 on 2025-02-20, dose reduced 2025-03-13) and PR-04 (eGFR 88, no cap).

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.5 SGLT2 inhibitor precautions SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose. The reference guideline requires: 1. Teach the **sick-day rule** at initiation: stop the drug during vomiting, fever, diarrhea, or poor oral intake, and for 3 days before elective surgery. 2. Check ketones if unwell even when glucose is not high. 3. After an episode of ketoacidosis attributed to an SGLT2 inhibitor, **do not re-challenge** with the drug class (MP-02). PAT-004 (PR-04) developed ketoacidosis on 2025-12-09 after not following the sick-day rule; empagliflozin was permanently stopped and recorded as an adverse drug reaction.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DIS-013)

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Diagnosis Diagnose when all are present: (1) beta-hydroxybutyrate (LAB-028) of **3.0 mmol/L or higher**; (2) venous or arterial pH below 7.30 or bicarbonate below 18 mmol/L (LAB-018, LAB-002); (3) diabetes or known risk. The **euglycemic variant** is diagnosed when glucose is below 14 mmol/L (250 mg/dL) with the same ketone and acid-base criteria; the SGLT2 inhibitor is the usual cause. Severity: mild pH 7.25 to 7.29; moderate 7.00 to 7.24; severe below 7.00. PAT-004 presented with pH 7.18 (moderate).

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Management | Component | Reference rule | |---|---| | Fluids | Isotonic fluid resuscitation first | | Potassium | Check potassium (LAB-005) before insulin. If below 3.3 mmol/L, replace first and delay insulin. If 3.3 to 5.2 mmol/L, give replacement with the insulin infusion | | Insulin | Insulin regular (MED-003) IV infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hour; add dextrose when glucose falls below 14 mmol/L in the typical form, or earlier in the euglycemic form | | Monitoring | Beta-hydroxybutyrate and glucose hourly initially, then every 2 hours; potassium every 2 to 4 hours | | Hypoglycemia | Glucose below the alert threshold needs dextrose added and the infusion rate reviewed | | Transition | Switch to subcutaneous insulin when ketones have cleared, with **basal insulin given at least 2 hours before the infusion is stopped** |

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Resolution criterion The reference guideline defines resolution of ketoacidosis as beta-hydroxybutyrate below 0.6 mmol/L. MediCore requires this on **two consecutive checks** before transition (MediCore Policy, FPA-12, PRO-010, HO-02), and defines its hypoglycemia alert at a glucose below 4.0 mmol/L (72 mg/dL).

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Application PAT-004: ketones fell from 5.4 to 0.4 mmol/L over 20 hours; the criterion was first met at 16:00 on 2025-12-10 (PR-04); glargine was given at 16:30 and the infusion stopped at 18:30, a 2-hour overlap.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Hyperlipidemia (DIS-014)

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Diagnosis and risk categories The lipid panel (LAB-009) is used. LDL-cholesterol targets by risk category: | Risk category | LDL-C target | |---|---| | Established atherosclerotic disease (for example after ACS) | below 1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) | | High risk (diabetes with CKD or multiple risk factors) | below 1.8 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) | | Moderate risk | below 2.6 mmol/L (100 mg/dL) |

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Treatment Atorvastatin (MED-009) is first line: 40 mg daily for high risk, 80 mg daily after ACS. Recheck lipids 6 to 8 weeks after starting or changing the dose. Report muscle symptoms. PAT-008 (PR-07) started 80 mg after NSTEMI; PAT-001 (PR-01) takes 40 mg.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 6. Hypothyroidism (DIS-016)

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.1 Diagnosis TSH (LAB-017) above the upper limit of the reference interval (**0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L**, LD-01) with low or low-normal free thyroxine.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.2 Treatment Levothyroxine (MED-024), starting at 1.6 micrograms/kg/day in healthy adults (25 to 50 micrograms in older patients or those with heart disease). Take once daily on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.3 Interactions that reduce absorption Oral iron, calcium, and antacids must be separated from levothyroxine by **at least 4 hours** (MediCore Policy FPA-14; MP-02, MP-06). If a new interacting drug is started, recheck TSH after 6 to 8 weeks.

title: Endocrine and Metabolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.4 Interpreting TSH Acute illness can transiently alter TSH; avoid dose changes on a single value during illness (PAT-004: TSH 4.1 mIU/L during ketoacidosis, 3.8 on 2026-03-18). Persistent elevation after a new co-medication suggests an absorption problem rather than disease progression (PAT-014: TSH 2.4, then 8.9 after iron was taken 30 minutes after levothyroxine, then 3.2 after separation; PR-08).

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline defines kidney-function staging, acute kidney injury staging, nephrotoxin avoidance, and the hyperkalemia algorithm. It is the clinical basis for renal dose adjustment (PRO-008, HO-02) and critical potassium calling (PRO-009, HO-05). Charts applying it: PR-01, PR-07 (PAT-009), PR-08 (PAT-011, PAT-013).

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Chronic Kidney Disease (DIS-003)

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Definition and staging CKD is present when eGFR (LAB-004) is below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 for at least 3 months, or when markers of kidney damage persist for 3 months. | Stage | eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) | |---|---| | G1 | 90 or higher (with kidney damage) | | G2 | 60 to 89 (with kidney damage) | | G3a | 45 to 59 | | **G3b** | **30 to 44** | | G4 | 15 to 29 | | G5 | below 15 | PAT-001 (eGFR 38 to 44) and PAT-009 (baseline eGFR 40) are stage G3b.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Drug and dose consequences - **Metformin (MED-001):** maximum 1,000 mg/day at eGFR 30 to 44; stop below 30 (also in DG-02, MP-02; protocol PRO-008). - **NSAIDs including ibuprofen (MED-026):** avoid in CKD (MP-05). Acetaminophen (MED-027) is the preferred analgesic. - **ACE inhibitor (MED-004) and spironolactone (MED-008):** permitted with monitoring; check potassium and creatinine at 1 week and 4 weeks after starting or increasing (DG-01). - **Other agents:** renal tiers for MED-004, 007, 008, 012, 015, 018, 019, 020 and 030 are tabulated in MP-07.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Monitoring Review eGFR at least every 6 months in G3b, and after any acute illness. Counsel patients to avoid potassium-based salt substitutes when taking an ACE inhibitor or spironolactone (PR-01).

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Acute Kidney Injury (DIS-017)

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Definition AKI is diagnosed by any of: serum creatinine rise of 26.5 umol/L (0.3 mg/dL) or more within 48 hours; creatinine at least 1.5 times baseline within 7 days; or urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/hour for 6 hours.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Staging by creatinine | Stage | Creatinine criterion | |---|---| | Stage 1 | 1.5 to 1.9 times baseline, or a rise of 26.5 umol/L (0.3 mg/dL) or more | | **Stage 2** | **2.0 to 2.9 times baseline** | | Stage 3 | 3.0 times baseline or more, or creatinine 354 umol/L (4.0 mg/dL) or more, or renal replacement therapy | Worked examples: PAT-009 baseline 1.3 mg/dL, peak 2.9 mg/dL = 2.2 times, stage 2 (PR-07); PAT-013 baseline 1.0 mg/dL, peak 2.3 mg/dL = 2.3 times, stage 2 (PR-08).

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Causes and nephrotoxin avoidance Evaluate prerenal causes (volume depletion), renal causes (nephrotoxins, sepsis), and post-renal obstruction. Key nephrotoxin hazards in this dataset: - **NSAIDs with an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic**, the "triple combination," in a patient with CKD (PAT-009). - **Vancomycin with piperacillin-tazobactam** (MP-06, MP-04), requiring pharmacy-managed dosing and early level checks (PAT-013). - Dehydration during infection, with diuretics and ACE inhibitors continued.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Management Stop or hold nephrotoxic and renally cleared drugs (ibuprofen, lisinopril, furosemide, metformin as applicable); restore volume; treat infection; relieve obstruction; recheck creatinine daily; adjust drug doses to current eGFR using MP-07. Resume ACE inhibitor and diuretic only after creatinine plateaus and oral intake is normal (PAT-009 resumed on 2026-03-31).

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Hyperkalemia (DIS-019)

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Reference guideline severity classes | Class | Potassium (LAB-005) | |---|---| | Mild | 5.5 to 5.9 mmol/L | | Moderate | 6.0 to 6.4 mmol/L | | Severe | 6.5 mmol/L or higher | **Distinction from MediCore Policy:** the laboratory *critical value* that triggers an urgent telephone call is set separately by MediCore Policy at **6.2 mmol/L or higher or 2.9 mmol/L or lower** (FPA-01; HO-05). The two systems are intentionally different: a result of 6.4 mmol/L is "moderate" in this guideline and "critical" under MediCore Policy.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Algorithm 1. Obtain a 12-lead ECG (LAB-021) and repeat the sample if hemolysis is suspected. 2. If ECG changes (peaked T waves, prolonged PR or QRS) or potassium is 6.2 mmol/L or higher: give IV calcium for membrane stabilization. 3. Shift potassium into cells: insulin regular 10 units IV with 25 g dextrose (MED-003). 4. Remove the cause: stop or hold spironolactone (MED-008) and the ACE inhibitor (MED-004); stop potassium supplements and salt substitutes; continue the loop diuretic (MED-007) if the patient is not volume-depleted. 5. Recheck potassium at 1 to 2 hours and then every 4 to 6 hours until below 5.5 mmol/L. 6. Before restarting an ACE inhibitor or MRA, potassium should be below 5.0 mmol/L, with a 1-week and 4-week recheck after the restart; a restart at a reduced dose is acceptable.

title: Renal and Electrolyte Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.3 Application PAT-001 presented on 2025-09-17 with potassium 6.4 mmol/L and ECG changes after three days of vomiting and diarrhea during which the sick-day rule (DG-01) was not followed (PR-01). Spironolactone, lisinopril, furosemide and metformin were held; lisinopril restarted at 5 mg on 2025-09-26 and spironolactone resumed at 12.5 mg on 2025-10-23 with 1-week and 4-week potassium checks. The telephone-notification delay for the result produced INC-002 (HO-08).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline gives diagnostic criteria, severity classes, and treatment steps for three respiratory conditions. The patient applications are PAT-003 (PR-03), PAT-005 (PR-05), PAT-007 (PR-07) and PAT-012 (PR-08). Antibiotic duration and sepsis management are owned by DG-05.

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (DIS-007)

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Diagnosis Spirometry (LAB-019) is required: a **post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70** confirms persistent airflow limitation in a patient with symptoms and risk factors (tobacco, occupational exposure).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Severity by FEV1 (percent predicted) | Class | FEV1 | |---|---| | Mild | 80% or higher | | Moderate | 50% to 79% | | Severe | 30% to 49% | | Very severe | below 30% | PAT-003 had FEV1/FVC 0.54 and FEV1 48% of predicted on 2024-11-20: **severe** COPD (PR-03, LD-08).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Maintenance treatment Long-acting antimuscarinic: tiotropium 18 micrograms inhaled daily (MED-022). Short-acting beta-agonist: albuterol as needed (MED-021). Smoking cessation and pulmonary rehabilitation are mandatory elements of care.

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.4 Acute exacerbation Triggers: increased dyspnea, sputum volume, or purulence. | Component | Reference rule | |---|---| | Bronchodilator | Albuterol nebulization every 4 hours initially (MED-021) | | Corticosteroid | Prednisone 40 mg daily for **5 days** (MED-023) | | Antibiotic | When sputum is purulent or there is radiographic pneumonia | | Oxygen | Controlled oxygen, target SpO2 88% to 92% | | Non-invasive ventilation | Indicated when arterial pH is **below 7.35 with PaCO2 above 6.0 kPa (45 mmHg)** despite initial treatment (LAB-018) | PAT-003 arrived with pH 7.28 and PaCO2 8.3 kPa and received non-invasive ventilation (PR-03).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Community-Acquired Pneumonia (DIS-008)

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Diagnosis Clinical features (fever, cough, pleuritic pain, new crackles) plus a new infiltrate on chest X-ray (LAB-020, LD-07). Procalcitonin (LAB-015) and C-reactive protein (LAB-016) support bacterial infection but do not replace imaging.

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Severity classes | Class | Criteria | |---|---| | Non-severe | None of the severe features | | **Severe** | Any of: respiratory rate 30 or higher; systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg; new confusion; sepsis (DG-05); need for ICU care | PAT-003 met severe criteria (respiratory rate 30, sepsis, later ICU); PAT-012 was non-severe (PR-08).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Antibiotic choice | Class | First-line agent | Notes | |---|---|---| | Non-severe | Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily (MED-016) | Not for patients with a penicillin allergy (ALG-001); see MP-07 for alternatives | | Severe | Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily (MED-017), with escalation per sepsis guideline (DG-05) | Obtain blood cultures (LAB-012) before the first dose |

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Duration and de-escalation Duration is set in **DG-05**: non-severe pneumonia, a minimum of 5 days; severe or bacteremic pneumococcal pneumonia, 7 days. The stewardship stop rule (procalcitonin below 0.25 ng/mL and afebrile for 48 hours at day 5) is MediCore Policy in HO-04 (PRO-013), not a guideline rule.

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.5 Follow-up Repeat chest X-ray at 6 weeks in patients over 50 or smokers to confirm resolution. PAT-003 and PAT-012 both had follow-up films (PR-03, PR-08).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Asthma (DIS-015)

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Diagnosis Variable respiratory symptoms plus reversible airflow limitation: FEV1 improvement of **12% and 200 mL or more** after bronchodilator on spirometry (LAB-019). PAT-007 showed 14% reversibility with FEV1 82% of predicted (PR-07, LD-08).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Control and treatment Short-acting beta-agonist (albuterol, MED-021) for symptoms; inhaled corticosteroid for persistent symptoms. Exacerbations: albuterol nebulization, prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days (MED-023).

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.3 NSAID- and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease In some patients with asthma, aspirin and other NSAIDs provoke bronchospasm, urticaria, or facial swelling (ALG-003). These drugs must be avoided entirely; the definition and cross-reactivity are in MP-07. PAT-005 has this pattern (PR-05). A beta-blocker (MED-006) is a caution in asthma; cardioselective agents are used with monitoring when indicated.

title: Respiratory Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.4 Antibiotics in an asthma exacerbation Antibiotics are not routinely required. A beta-lactam given to a patient with a penicillin allergy flag requires the dual-verification step (MediCore Policy PRO-003, FPA-09, HO-02). The failure of that step in PAT-007 is documented in PR-07 and HO-08 (INC-001).

section: DG-05: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: # DG-05: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference) > **SYNTHETIC DATA NOTICE.** This document is a fictional reference guideline written for software benchmarking and education. Its criteria, thresholds, and algorithms are invented, may differ from real-world practice, and must not be used for clinical decisions. "Reference Guideline" statements are kept separate from "MediCore Policy" statements owned by the HO documents.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 1. Document Control | Field | Value | |---|---| | Document ID | DG-05 | | Folder | 02_Diseases_Clinical_Guidelines | | Version / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-01 | | Conditions covered | Sepsis (DIS-009), complicated urinary tract infection (DIS-010), C. difficile infection (DIS-023); pneumonia antibiotic durations (DIS-008) | | Owner | Infectious Diseases (DEP-007, head STF-009), approved by the CPRB and the Antimicrobial Stewardship Committee (ASC) | | Companion documents | DG-04, MP-04, MP-06, LD-04, LD-05, HO-03, HO-04, HO-06 |

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline sets the clinical rules for recognizing sepsis, choosing and stopping antibiotics, and treating two common infections and one antibiotic-associated infection. MediCore time targets (sepsis bundle, isolation duration, stewardship stop rule) are **policies** in HO-03, HO-04 and HO-06; this document refers to them but does not set their values.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Sepsis (DIS-009)

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Recognition Sepsis is suspected infection with acute organ dysfunction. Screening triggers: temperature above 38.0 C or below 36.0 C, heart rate above 100, respiratory rate 22 or higher, systolic pressure 100 mmHg or below, altered mentation, or lactate (LAB-014) above 2.0 mmol/L.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Initial management | Step | Reference guideline statement | |---|---| | Cultures | Blood cultures (LAB-012), two sets, **before** antibiotics when this causes no delay; urine culture (LAB-013) when a urinary source is possible | | Antibiotics | First dose as soon as possible after recognition and within one hour. The MediCore time target and its versions are in PRO-004 (HO-03) | | Lactate | Measure at recognition and repeat when elevated; the MediCore repeat rule is in PRO-004 | | Fluids | Crystalloid resuscitation for hypotension or lactate of 4 mmol/L or higher | | Source control | Drain or remove infected collections or obstruction promptly |

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Choice of antibiotics Empiric cover is based on the source, local susceptibility, and allergy status (MP-07). For severe sepsis from pneumonia, ceftriaxone (MED-017) is the starting agent, with escalation to piperacillin-tazobactam (MED-018) plus vancomycin (MED-019) for deterioration or when resistant gram-positive organisms are possible (PAT-003, PR-03). For a urinary source with obstruction, piperacillin-tazobactam (MED-018) is used (PAT-013, PR-08).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.4 Monitoring antibiotic toxicity Vancomycin is pharmacy-managed. Draw the **first level before the fourth dose** (MediCore Policy FPA-11, PRO-013). Vancomycin combined with piperacillin-tazobactam carries a recognized nephrotoxicity risk (MP-06); dose to current eGFR and reduce piperacillin-tazobactam at eGFR 30 or below (MP-07, PRO-008).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.5 De-escalation Review at 48 to 72 hours. When susceptibilities are known, narrow to the most selective effective agent and stop vancomycin if no resistant gram-positive organism is isolated. PAT-003 was de-escalated within 5 hours of the susceptibility report (PR-03); PAT-013 had vancomycin stopped at 48 hours (PR-08).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.6 Procalcitonin Procalcitonin (LAB-015) supports stopping antibiotics when it falls below **0.25 ng/mL** or by 80% from peak, together with clinical recovery. The binding stewardship stop rule is MediCore Policy in HO-04.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Antibiotic Duration Summary (Reference Guideline) | Infection | Duration | |---|---| | Non-severe community-acquired pneumonia (DIS-008) | Minimum **5 days**, if afebrile and clinically stable for 48 hours | | Severe or bacteremic pneumococcal pneumonia | **7 days** | | Complicated UTI (DIS-010) | **7 days** with clinical response | | C. difficile infection (DIS-023) | **10 days** of oral vancomycin | Applied: PAT-012, 5 days (PR-08); PAT-003, 7 days (PR-03); PAT-013, 7 days (PR-08); PAT-003 oral vancomycin, 10 days (PR-03). PAT-006 received only 5 days of ciprofloxacin because of an interaction event; stewardship accepted this with documented symptom resolution and a negative follow-up culture (PR-06).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Complicated Urinary Tract Infection (DIS-010)

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Definition UTI with fever or systemic features, obstruction, recent hospitalization or instrumentation, immunosuppression, or other conditions that raise treatment failure risk. Diagnosis by urinalysis and culture (LAB-013).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Treatment | Setting | Options | |---|---| | Oral, culture-susceptible | Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily (MED-020) | | Parenteral | Ceftriaxone (MED-017) or piperacillin-tazobactam (MED-018) | | Penicillin allergy (ALG-001) | Avoid MED-016 and MED-018; ciprofloxacin or a cephalosporin under MP-07 rules |

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.3 Interaction with anticoagulants Ciprofloxacin raises the INR in patients taking warfarin (MED-013); check INR within the interval specified in PRO-007 (HO-04) or choose a non-interacting agent (MP-06, MP-04). PAT-006 illustrates the consequence of an unplanned interaction (INR 6.8, INC-003, PR-06).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.4 Source control Relieve obstruction (catheter or stent) in obstructed infection; PAT-013 had a urinary catheter placed with 650 mL drained (PR-08).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 6. Clostridioides difficile Infection (DIS-023)

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.1 Diagnosis Test (LAB-024) when there are three or more unformed stools in 24 hours without another cause and typically after recent antibiotics or hospitalization. A positive toxin or PCR in a symptomatic patient is diagnostic.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.2 Severity Severe when white cell count exceeds 15 x 10^9/L or creatinine exceeds 1.5 times baseline.

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.3 Treatment Stop the inciting antibiotic if possible. First episode: **vancomycin 125 mg orally every 6 hours for 10 days** (MED-019, oral route; MP-04). PAT-003 received this regimen from 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-16 (PR-03).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 6.4 Infection prevention Contact-enteric precautions and dedicated equipment. The MediCore isolation duration (72 hours after diarrhea resolves) is policy FPA-10 in PRO-012 (HO-06). Delay in starting precautions is reported as an incident (INC-004, HO-08).

title: Infection and Sepsis Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 7. Its criteria, thresholds, and algorithms are invented, may differ from real-world practice, and must not be used for clinical decisions. "Reference Guideline" statements are kept separate from "MediCore Policy" statements owned by the HO documents.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 1. Document Control | Field | Value | |---|---| | Document ID | DG-06 | | Folder | 02_Diseases_Clinical_Guidelines | | Version / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-01 | | Conditions covered | Acute ischemic stroke (DIS-011), venous thromboembolism (DIS-012), and the AF-stroke link (DIS-005) | | Owner | Neurology (DEP-008, head STF-010) with Internal Medicine (DEP-002), approved by the CPRB | | Companion documents | DG-01, MP-03, MP-06, MP-07, LD-02, LD-06, LD-07, HO-03, HO-04 |

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline covers diagnosis and secondary prevention after ischemic stroke and the diagnosis and anticoagulant treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Time-critical steps for stroke (door-to-CT) are MediCore Policy in PRO-005 (HO-03) and are not set here. The charts that apply it are PR-05 and PR-06.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Acute Ischemic Stroke (DIS-011)

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Initial assessment Establish last known well time. Score severity with the NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS). Obtain non-contrast CT head (LAB-022) to exclude hemorrhage before any antithrombotic treatment. Record a 12-lead ECG (LAB-021) and complete blood count (LAB-001), PT/INR (LAB-010) and glucose. The time target for CT is in PRO-005 (HO-03, FPA-07).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Reperfusion decision Reperfusion therapy is decided by the stroke team (DEP-008) based on last known well, imaging and deficit. It is not recommended when deficits are minor or rapidly resolving. The agents involved are outside the dataset formulary; the decision and its rationale must be documented (PR-05).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Etiology work-up Echocardiography (LAB-023) and rhythm assessment for a cardioembolic source. New atrial fibrillation (DIS-005) found after stroke is treated as the likely cause.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.4 Secondary prevention: antiplatelet therapy Aspirin 300 mg then 75 to 100 mg daily (MED-010) is the first-line antiplatelet. **If aspirin is contraindicated** (for example NSAID/aspirin hypersensitivity, ALG-003), use **clopidogrel** (MED-011) 300 mg loading dose then 75 mg daily (MP-03, MP-07). Do not use any NSAID (including ibuprofen, MED-026) in a patient with ALG-003.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 3.5 Secondary prevention: anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation
text: ### 3.5 Secondary prevention: anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation Anticoagulation (apixaban, MED-012) is started after stroke with AF at a time determined by stroke severity and imaging: | Initial NIHSS | Earliest start of anticoagulant (counting day 0 as the day of onset) | |---|---| | Below 5 (mild) | Day 2 | | **5 to 15 (moderate)** | **Between day 4 and day 7**, provided **repeat CT (LAB-022) shows no hemorrhagic transformation** | | Above 15 (severe) | Day 10 to day 14 | When the anticoagulant starts, the antiplatelet agent is stopped unless a separate indication exists. Pharmacist verification of the new apixaban order within 4 hours is MediCore Policy (FPA-04, PRO-007, HO-04). PAT-005 started apixaban on day 5, with clopidogrel stopped (PR-05).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.6 Other secondary prevention Statin therapy (DG-02), blood-pressure reduction to below 130/80 mmHg after the acute phase (DG-01), glucose control, smoking cessation, rehabilitation.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Venous Thromboembolism (DIS-012)

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Diagnosis 1. Estimate clinical pre-test probability. 2. If low or intermediate probability, measure D-dimer (LAB-026). A normal D-dimer excludes VTE; an elevated value requires imaging. 3. Confirm PE by CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA, LAB-027) or leg ultrasound for DVT. PAT-006: D-dimer 3,850 ng/mL FEU, followed by CTPA showing right lower lobe segmental emboli (PR-06, LD-02, LD-07).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Parenteral anticoagulation - Unfractionated heparin infusion (MED-014) with aPTT (LAB-011) target **60 to 80 seconds** when rapid reversibility is desirable or renal function is poor. - Enoxaparin (MED-015) 1 mg per kg subcutaneously every 12 hours when the patient is stable; reduce or avoid when eGFR is below 30 (MP-07, PRO-008).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Transition to warfarin Start warfarin (MED-013) on day 1 (the day after heparin starts) with target INR 2.0 to 3.0. Continue parenteral therapy for **at least 5 days and until INR is 2.0 or higher on two consecutive checks**. The MediCore protocol operationalizing this is PRO-007 (HO-04). PAT-006 had 10 days of parenteral cover (PR-06).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Alternative: apixaban Apixaban (MED-012) may be used for VTE when appropriate (MP-03); this was not the choice for PAT-006.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.5 Duration | Situation | Anticoagulation duration | |---|---| | **Provoked** by a major transient risk factor (for example surgery) | **3 months** | | Unprovoked | At least 6 months, then review | | Cancer-associated | Indefinite while cancer active | PAT-006 (provoked by knee replacement) completed 3 months on 2025-11-29 (PR-06).

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.6 Interacting drugs Many drugs raise or lower the INR. Ciprofloxacin (MED-020) raises it (MP-06). When an interacting drug is started, an INR recheck plan is required (PRO-007). NSAIDs are avoided during anticoagulation; acetaminophen (MED-027) is preferred.

title: Neurovascular and Thromboembolic Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. section: DG-07: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: # DG-07: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference) > **SYNTHETIC DATA NOTICE.** This document is a fictional reference guideline written for software benchmarking and education. Its criteria, thresholds, and algorithms are invented, may differ from real-world practice, and must not be used for clinical decisions. "Reference Guideline" statements are kept separate from "MediCore Policy" statements owned by the HO documents.

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 1. Document Control | Field | Value | |---|---| | Document ID | DG-07 | | Folder | 02_Diseases_Clinical_Guidelines | | Version / date | 1.0 / 2026-10-01 | | Conditions covered | Iron-deficiency anemia (DIS-018), upper GI bleeding (DIS-022), anaphylaxis and drug hypersensitivity (DIS-024) | | Owner | Internal Medicine (DEP-002) with Emergency Medicine (DEP-001), approved by the CPRB | | Companion documents | MP-02, MP-03, MP-05, MP-06, MP-07, LD-02, HO-02 |

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope This guideline sets diagnostic criteria and management steps for three conditions that recur across the patient charts: anemia from iron deficiency (PAT-002, PAT-014), gastrointestinal bleeding (PAT-002, PAT-010), and anaphylaxis (PAT-007).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Iron-Deficiency Anemia (DIS-018)

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Diagnostic criteria Both of the following: | Sex | Hemoglobin (LAB-001) | Ferritin (LAB-025) | |---|---|---| | Women | below **12.0 g/dL** | below **15 ng/mL** | | Men | below 13.0 g/dL | below 15 ng/mL | Supporting findings: low MCV, low transferrin saturation. Examples: PAT-014 (Hb 9.8 g/dL, ferritin 7 ng/mL, PR-08); PAT-002 (Hb 7.6 to 9.1 g/dL, ferritin 9 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 6%, PR-02).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Look for the source Investigate gastrointestinal blood loss in all men and in postmenopausal women; in premenopausal and perimenopausal women consider menstrual loss and, when indicated, endoscopy (PAT-014 had both endoscopies; PR-08).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Treatment Oral ferrous sulfate 325 mg once daily (MED-031), preferably with vitamin C and away from tea and coffee. Recheck hemoglobin at 4 weeks (expected rise of at least 1 g/dL). Continue for **3 months after hemoglobin normalizes** to restore stores. Intravenous iron is reserved for intolerance, malabsorption, or ongoing loss.

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.4 Interactions Ferrous sulfate reduces levothyroxine (MED-024) absorption: separate by **at least 4 hours** (MediCore Policy FPA-14; MP-02, MP-06). PAT-014 illustrates the TSH rise after co-administration (PR-08).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding (DIS-022)

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Presentation and assessment Melena or hematemesis, tachycardia, hypotension. Obtain CBC (LAB-001), PT/INR (LAB-010), ferritin (LAB-025) after resuscitation, type and screen. Review all antithrombotic and NSAID exposure including over-the-counter aspirin (PRO-001, HO-02).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Transfusion Transfuse red cells when hemoglobin is below **7 g/dL**, or below **8 g/dL in patients with cardiovascular disease**. PAT-002 (coronary stent, Hb 7.6 g/dL) was transfused two units; PAT-010 (Hb 8.8 g/dL, no cardiovascular disease) was not (PR-02, PR-07).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.3 Acid suppression Proton pump inhibitor: pantoprazole (MED-028). For ulcers with high-risk stigmata (visible vessel, active bleeding): 80 mg IV bolus then 40 mg every 12 hours. For low-risk ulcers (clean base): 40 mg IV every 12 hours. Continue 40 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, then once daily for as long as antithrombotic therapy continues (MP-02).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.4 Endoscopy Within 24 hours of presentation after resuscitation. Test for Helicobacter pylori (stool antigen or biopsy) and treat if positive. Repeat endoscopy for healing is advised for ulcers with a visible vessel or when requested by gastroenterology (PAT-002, repeat 2025-08-12).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.5 Managing antithrombotic drugs during bleeding | Drug | Rule | |---|---| | Anticoagulant (apixaban, MED-012) | Hold. Resume 3 to 7 days after endoscopic hemostasis once hemoglobin has been stable for 48 hours. Pharmacist verifies the new order within 4 hours (FPA-04) | | P2Y12 inhibitor (clopidogrel, MED-011) with a coronary stent placed within the last 6 months | **Continue** by joint decision of cardiology and gastroenterology | | Aspirin (MED-010) and NSAIDs (MED-026) | Stop; do not restart NSAIDs | PAT-002: apixaban held 2025-05-19 to 2025-05-23 (resumed day 4); clopidogrel continued because the stent was 11 weeks old (PR-02).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.6 Preventing recurrence Avoid NSAIDs; use acetaminophen (MED-027). An SSRI (MED-025) also raises bleeding risk. After an NSAID- or aspirin-associated bleed in a patient on an SSRI, follow DG-08 (stop NSAID and aspirin; continue the SSRI with a PPI if depression is stable). PAT-010 (PR-07).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Anaphylaxis and Drug Hypersensitivity (DIS-024)

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Diagnosis Acute onset of skin or mucosal involvement (urticaria, flushing, lip swelling) together with respiratory compromise or hypotension, or hypotension alone after exposure to a likely allergen.

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 First-line treatment | Step | Rule | |---|---| | Remove trigger | Stop the suspected drug | | **Epinephrine (MED-029)** | **0.5 mg intramuscular** into the anterolateral thigh in adults; **repeat every 5 to 15 minutes** if there is no improvement | | Position and fluids | Lie flat, raise legs; IV crystalloid for hypotension | | Adjuncts | Nebulized albuterol (MED-021) for wheeze | | Observation | Minimum 6 hours; extend to **24 hours** when two or more epinephrine doses were needed | PAT-007 received epinephrine 0.5 mg IM at 21:19 and again at 21:27 (8 minutes later) and was observed 24 hours (PR-07).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.3 After the event Prescribe an epinephrine auto-injector (MED-029) and teach use; update the allergy record with the confirmed reaction and severity; refer to allergy services; add cephalosporin cross-reactivity precautions where relevant (MP-07).

title: Hematology, GI and Hypersensitivity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.4 Allergy documentation An allergy entry without verification, such as "rash, patient-reported, unverified," must not be treated as low risk. Before the first dose of a beta-lactam in any patient with an allergy flag, MediCore requires **dual verification** by pharmacist and nurse (PRO-003, FPA-09, HO-02). The failure of this step is the subject of INC-001 (HO-08).

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 2. Purpose and Scope Patients seldom have one disease. This guideline covers two chronic conditions that frequently conflict with other treatments and supplies the **conflict rules** that tell clinicians which drug to avoid in which disease, and what to use instead. It is the hub document for medication-versus-condition conflicts in the dataset.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 3. Major Depressive Disorder (DIS-020)

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.1 Diagnosis Five or more depressive symptoms for at least two weeks with functional impairment, supported by a PHQ-9 score of **10 or higher**.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.2 Treatment Psychotherapy and/or an SSRI. Sertraline (MED-025) 50 mg daily, titrated to 100 to 200 mg. Review response at 4 to 6 weeks. Continue for at least 6 months after remission.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.3 Bleeding risk with SSRIs SSRIs impair platelet function. The risk of gastrointestinal bleeding rises when an SSRI is combined with an NSAID (MED-026), aspirin (MED-010) or an anticoagulant. MP-06 rates the combination of sertraline with ibuprofen and aspirin as **Major**.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 3.4 After a bleed After an NSAID- or aspirin-associated bleed in a patient on sertraline whose depression is stable: **stop the NSAID and the aspirin permanently, continue sertraline, and add a proton pump inhibitor** (MED-028) for as long as bleeding risk persists (DG-07). Switching an SSRI during a stable remission is not required. PAT-010 followed this rule (PR-07).

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 4. Osteoarthritis (DIS-021)

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.1 Diagnosis Clinical: age over 45, activity-related joint pain, brief morning stiffness, bony enlargement; imaging when needed.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 4.2 Treatment ladder | Step | Intervention | |---|---| | 1 | Exercise, weight management, physiotherapy | | 2 | **Acetaminophen** (MED-027) up to 3 g per day | | 3 | Topical agents | | 4 | Oral NSAID (ibuprofen, MED-026), only when none of the contraindications in 4.3 applies, at the lowest dose and shortest duration | | 5 | Joint injection or replacement |

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
section: 4.3 When an NSAID must not be used
text: ### 4.3 When an NSAID must not be used Avoid oral NSAIDs in: chronic kidney disease or AKI (DG-03); anticoagulant therapy (DG-06); a history of gastrointestinal bleeding (DG-07); concurrent SSRI plus antiplatelet (section 3); heart failure; NSAID/aspirin hypersensitivity (ALG-003, MP-07). Where any applies, remain at step 2. PAT-009 (CKD G3b) was prescribed ibuprofen against this rule and developed AKI (INC-005, PR-07). PAT-006 (anticoagulated) used acetaminophen (PR-06). PAT-010 developed a bleed on ibuprofen with aspirin and sertraline (PR-07).

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ## 5. Polypharmacy Review

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.1 Definition Polypharmacy is five or more regular medicines. Patients in this dataset with polypharmacy include PAT-001 (six), PAT-002 (seven), PAT-009 and PAT-010.

title: Chronic Disease and Multimorbidity Guidelines (Fictional Reference)
text: ### 5.2 Method At each admission and discharge and at periodic outpatient review (the MediCore reconciliation protocol is PRO-001, HO-02): 1. List every medicine including over-the-counter and supplements (PAT-010 took aspirin 81 mg unrecorded). 2. Match each to an active indication. 3. Check each against kidney function (MP-07). 4. Check each pair against MP-06. 5. Check each against documented allergies (ALG entities, MP-07). 6. Stop or reduce anything without an indication.

section: 2.2 Penicillin to cephalosporin cross-reactivity (rule for ceftriaxone)
text: ### 2.2 Penicillin to cephalosporin cross-reactivity (rule for ceftriaxone) | Prior penicillin reaction | Ceftriaxone (MED-017) | |---|---| | Non-severe (for example urticaria without airway or circulatory involvement) | Permitted; **dual verification by pharmacist and nurse** for the first dose (PRO-003, FPA-09) | | Severe (anaphylaxis, angioedema, severe cutaneous reaction) | **Avoid** until allergy evaluation or a supervised graded challenge | | Unverified, patient-reported | Treated as the **worst credible reaction** until verified; an unverified flag must not be treated as low risk (DG-07) | PAT-006 (non-severe urticaria) could receive ceftriaxone under this rule but was prescribed ciprofloxacin (PR-06). PAT-007 (anaphylaxis) must avoid ceftriaxone until allergy evaluation.

title: Allergy, ADR and Organ-Function Dosing Reference
text: ### 2.3 Allergy record standard Each allergy entry records: allergen class (ALG), reaction, severity, date, verification status (verified or unverified), and source. After an event the record is updated the same day. Dual verification before the first dose of any beta-lactam in a patient with **any** allergy flag is MediCore Policy (FPA-09, PRO-003).

title: Allergy, ADR and Organ-Function Dosing Reference
text: ### 4.1 General tier labels Tier labels are used in PRO-008 (HO-02) and in this document. eGFR is in mL/min/1.73 m2. | Tier | eGFR | |---|---| | Tier 1 | 60 or higher | | Tier 2 | 45 to 59 | | Tier 3 | 30 to 44 (CKD stage G3b) | | Tier 4 | 15 to 29 | | Tier 5 | below 15 |
