section: 4.2 Drug-specific rules (the thresholds below take precedence over tier labels)
text: ### 4.2 Drug-specific rules (the thresholds below take precedence over tier labels) | Drug | Rule | |---|---| | MED-001 metformin | **Tier 1 and 2: no cap. Tier 3 (30 to 44): maximum 1,000 mg/day. Below 30: stop** (FPA-03) | | MED-004 lisinopril | Tier 3: start 2.5 to 5 mg, maximum 20 mg/day. Tier 4: start 2.5 mg, maximum 10 mg/day, specialist. Tier 5: avoid unless nephrology agrees | | MED-007 furosemide | No reduction; larger doses may be required at low eGFR | | MED-008 spironolactone | eGFR 45 or higher: start 25 mg. 30 to 44: start 12.5 mg. Below 30: avoid | | MED-012 apixaban | 2.5 mg twice daily if at least two of: age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or higher. Avoid below eGFR 15 | | MED-015 enoxaparin | eGFR below 30: 1 mg/kg once daily, or use unfractionated heparin | | MED-016 amoxicillin-clavulanate | Avoid the 875 mg tablet below eGFR 30 | | MED-018 piperacillin-tazobactam | **eGFR above 30: 4.5 g every 6 hours. eGFR 30 or below: 3.375 g every 6 hours** | | MED-019 vancomycin IV | Pharmacy-managed by levels; interval extended as eGFR falls; first level before the fourth dose (FPA-11) | | MED-020 ciprofloxacin | eGFR 30 to 50: 250 to 500 mg every 12 hours; below 30: every 18 to 24 hours | | MED-026 ibuprofen | Avoid in CKD stages G3 to G5 and in AKI | | MED-030 empagliflozin | Do not start below eGFR 20; reduced glucose lowering below 45 | | MED-002 / MED-003 insulin | Reduced clearance; lower starting doses and watch for hypoglycemia | | Other formulary drugs | No renal adjustment |

Every time target, threshold, and rule is an invented parameter that may differ from real practice and must not be used for clinical decisions.

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ## 2. PRO-001: Medication Reconciliation (version 2, effective 2024-06-01) 1. A pharmacist or trained technician obtains a **best possible medication history** within **24 hours of admission**, from at least two sources, and **explicitly includes over-the-counter drugs, supplements, and potassium-containing salt substitutes**. 2. Every medicine is matched to an active indication, kidney function (MP-07), documented allergies (MP-07), and interaction rules (MP-06). 3. At discharge a reconciled list is given to the patient and sent to the primary physician. 4. Patients taking five or more regular medicines receive a structured pharmacist review at least every **90 days** in outpatient care (DG-08). 5. Reconciliation findings that change therapy are recorded in the chart. Example: aspirin 81 mg taken over the counter by PAT-010 was found at the admission interview (PR-07).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ## 3. PRO-002: High-Alert Medication Safety (version 2, effective 2025-03-01) High-alert medications at MediCore are **MED-002, MED-003, MED-012, MED-013, MED-014, MED-015, MED-019, MED-029** (insulin glargine, insulin regular, apixaban, warfarin, unfractionated heparin, enoxaparin, vancomycin, epinephrine). | Rule | Requirement | |---|---| | Ordering | Structured order sets only; dose and weight displayed | | Verification | Pharmacist verification before dispensing; for MED-012 within **4 hours** of a new order (FPA-04, PRO-007) | | Administration | Independent double check by two nurses for insulin infusions, heparin infusions, and IV vancomycin; epinephrine for anaphylaxis is exempt from pre-administration double check but is reviewed afterward | | Storage | Separate labeled bins; no look-alike storage | | Monitoring | Drug-specific (HO-04 for anticoagulants and vancomycin; section 6 for insulin) |

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
section: 4. PRO-003: Allergy Documentation and Alerts (version 2, effective 2026-07-01)
text: ## 4. PRO-003: Allergy Documentation and Alerts (version 2, effective 2026-07-01)

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 4.1 Allergy record Each flag records allergen class (ALG-001 to ALG-006), reaction, severity, date, **verification status**, and source. An **unverified or patient-reported flag is treated as the worst credible reaction** until verified (MP-07). The allergy is updated the same day after any event.

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 4.2 Dual verification (FPA-09) Before the **first dose of any beta-lactam** (MED-016, MED-017, MED-018 and any other penicillin or cephalosporin) in a patient with **any allergy flag**, **both a pharmacist and a nurse must independently verify** the allergy, the drug, and the cross-reactivity rule in MP-07. The two checks are recorded separately.

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 4.3 Version 2 change (after INC-001) In **version 1 (to 2026-06-30)** the bar-code "urgent override" could bypass the nursing check if the prescriber documented urgency. In **version 2 (from 2026-07-01)** the override is a **hard stop**: the nursing check cannot be bypassed for a first beta-lactam dose in a patient with an allergy flag. The event that triggered the change is INC-001 (PAT-007, 2026-05-17; PR-07, HO-08).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 4.4 Special flags - **ALG-005 (iodinated contrast):** flag is displayed to Radiology (DEP-012); the pre-medication pathway is chosen by Radiology and the prescriber. No patient currently carries this flag. - **ALG-006 (latex):** the patient's wristband and room are marked; latex-free gloves, catheters and tourniquets are supplied. Example: PAT-009 (PR-07). - **ALG-003 and ALG-004:** order sets must not default to aspirin or ACE inhibitors for flagged patients. A default aspirin order for PAT-005 was cancelled before administration on 2026-04-14 and logged as a near-miss (PR-05, HO-08).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ## 5. PRO-008: Renal Dose Adjustment (version 3, effective 2026-05-01) 1. Every inpatient order and every outpatient prescription for a drug in the MP-07 section 4.2 list is checked against the **most recent eGFR**. Pharmacy owns the check; Nephrology (DEP-005) advises. 2. **Metformin (FPA-03):** eGFR 45 or higher no cap; **eGFR 30 to 44 maximum 1,000 mg/day; eGFR below 30 stop** (MP-02, MP-07). 3. Other renal rules follow MP-07, including piperacillin-tazobactam (**3.375 g every 6 hours at eGFR 30 or below**), enoxaparin, lisinopril, spironolactone and apixaban. 4. A new eGFR that falls into a lower band triggers a **renal-dose alert**. In version 1 (to 2025-04-30) the alert went only to the pharmacist work queue; in **version 2 (2025-05-01 to 2026-04-30)** it also went to the prescriber's inbox; in **version 3 (from 2026-05-01)** it does both and in addition: - An **NSAID order (for example MED-026) at eGFR below 60 is a hard stop**; override requires a second pharmacist and a documented reason. 5. The metformin cap should be implemented within **14 days** of the qualifying eGFR. (PAT-001's cap was applied 21 days after the eGFR of 2025-02-20, during version 1 of this protocol, which routed the alert only to the pharmacist queue; PR-01.) 6. The change to version 3 followed INC-005 (PAT-009, ibuprofen prescribed 2026-03-05 with an overridden alert; PR-07, HO-08).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
section: 6. PRO-010: Hypoglycemia and Insulin Safety (version 2, effective 2025-01-01)
text: ## 6. PRO-010: Hypoglycemia and Insulin Safety (version 2, effective 2025-01-01)

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 6.1 Hypoglycemia alert (FPA-12) A glucose **below 4.0 mmol/L (72 mg/dL)** triggers an alert: confirm by capillary measurement, give treatment, recheck in 15 minutes, notify the prescriber. During an insulin infusion, **dextrose is added to the infusion** and the rate reviewed.

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 6.2 DKA insulin infusion transition (FPA-12) 1. Infusion of MED-003 at 0.1 units/kg/hour begins after the potassium rule in DG-02 is satisfied. 2. Beta-hydroxybutyrate (LAB-028) and glucose are checked hourly at first, then every 2 hours. 3. **Transition to subcutaneous insulin is permitted when beta-hydroxybutyrate is below 0.6 mmol/L on two consecutive checks.** 4. Give the first subcutaneous basal dose (MED-002) at least **2 hours before** the infusion is stopped. 5. Example: PAT-004 had values of 0.5 mmol/L at 14:00 and 0.4 at 16:00 on 2025-12-10, so the criterion was met at 16:00; glargine was given at 16:30 and the infusion stopped at 18:30 (PR-04, LD-03).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ### 6.3 SGLT2 inhibitors A patient prescribed MED-030 receives sick-day teaching at initiation, recorded in the chart (DG-02). After an episode of DKA the drug is recorded as an adverse reaction and cannot be reordered without a documented override (MP-02, MP-07).

title: Medication Safety Protocols Manual
text: ## 7. Override Audit Overridden **Major** interaction alerts and all overridden renal or allergy hard stops are audited monthly by Clinical Pharmacy (DEP-010) and reported to the PSC. Overrides involved in INC-001, INC-003 and INC-005 are recorded in HO-08.

text: ## 2. PRO-004: Sepsis Bundle

title: Time-Critical Care Pathways
section: 2.1 Version history (the version in force on the event date applies)
text: ### 2.1 Version history (the version in force on the event date applies) | Version | Effective | Superseded | First-antibiotic target (from sepsis alert) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2022-03-01 | 2024-12-31 | 90 minutes | | 2 | 2025-01-01 | 2026-02-28 | **60 minutes** | | **3** | **2026-03-01** | In force | **50 minutes** (FPA-02) |

title: Time-Critical Care Pathways
section: 2.2 Bundle elements (version 3; identical in version 2 except for the antibiotic target)
text: ### 2.2 Bundle elements (version 3; identical in version 2 except for the antibiotic target) 1. **Start event:** sepsis alert activated by the screening trigger (DG-05). 2. Measure lactate (LAB-014) at the alert; draw blood cultures (LAB-012) **before** the first antibiotic if this does not delay it. 3. **Give the first antibiotic within 50 minutes of the alert.** 4. Repeat lactate within **2 hours** if the first value is **above 2.5 mmol/L**. 5. Crystalloid resuscitation for hypotension or lactate of 4.0 mmol/L or higher. 6. Reassess and escalate through PRO-015 if mean arterial pressure stays below 65 mmHg. 7. Review cultures and de-escalate at 48 to 72 hours under PRO-013 (HO-04).

text: ### 5.1 Triggers (any one) Respiratory rate 30 or higher; heart rate above 130; systolic pressure below 90 mmHg or mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg; acute change in consciousness; staff concern.

title: Anticoagulation and Antimicrobial Stewardship Protocols
section: 2.2 Rules (apply to both versions unless stated)
text: ### 2.2 Rules (apply to both versions unless stated) | Rule | Requirement | |---|---| | New apixaban order | **Pharmacist verification within 4 hours** (FPA-04) | | Anticoagulant plus antiplatelet | Pharmacist review of every combination (DG-01) | | Default warfarin target | **INR 2.0 to 3.0** (FPA-05) | | Parenteral overlap | Continue heparin or enoxaparin for **at least 5 days and until INR is 2.0 or higher on two consecutive checks** (DG-06) | | INR below 2.0 | Increase weekly dose by 10 to 15% | | **INR above range up to 4.5** | Reduce weekly dose by about 10% and **recheck INR within 3 days** | | **INR above 4.5** | Hold 1 to 2 doses; **anticoagulation-clinic telephone call within 24 hours** (FPA-05); recheck the next day | | Critical INR | **5.0 or higher** is also a PRO-009 critical result, phoned within 20 minutes (HO-05) | | **After discharge** | **INR check within 72 hours of discharge** for every patient on warfarin (FPA-05); also scheduled in the discharge plan (PRO-011, HO-07) | | **Interacting drug started** | A **written INR recheck plan** must exist before the first dose of an interacting drug (MP-06), with an INR within 3 days; in version 2 this is enforced by the order screen | | Bleeding | Apixaban held; resumption 3 to 7 days after hemostasis once hemoglobin is stable for 48 hours, with pharmacist verification in 4 hours (DG-07) |

title: Anticoagulation and Antimicrobial Stewardship Protocols
text: ### 3.2 Rules (version 2) | Rule | Requirement | |---|---| | Cultures first | Blood cultures before the first antibiotic where feasible (PRO-004, HO-03) | | **Vancomycin levels (FPA-11)** | IV vancomycin is pharmacy-managed; the **first level is drawn before the fourth dose**. A level above 20 mg/L prompts holding the next dose and re-dosing by pharmacy (MP-04) | | **48-hour review** | Every broad-spectrum course is reviewed by stewardship at 48 hours. **IV vancomycin is stopped at 48 hours if no resistant gram-positive organism has been identified** | | De-escalation | When susceptibilities are available, narrow to the most selective effective agent; stewardship documents the decision within 24 hours of the report | | Duration | Follows DG-05: non-severe CAP minimum 5 days, severe or bacteremic pneumococcal pneumonia 7 days, complicated UTI 7 days, C. difficile 10 days | | **Procalcitonin stop rule (MediCore Policy)** | In non-severe pneumonia, antibiotics **may stop at day 5 when procalcitonin is below 0.25 ng/mL and the patient has been afebrile for at least 48 hours** | | Interaction check | Antibiotic orders are checked against MP-06 (for example ciprofloxacin with warfarin) |

text: ## 2. PRO-009: Critical Laboratory Value Notification

title: Laboratory Operations and Critical Results
text: ### 2.1 Version history | Version | Effective | Change | |---|---|---| | 1 | 2023-01-01 to 2025-10-31 | Call the responsible clinician or the ward or triage line | | **2** | **2025-11-01** | After **two unanswered or busy attempts** the call **escalates automatically to the responsible clinician's pager** (after INC-002) |

title: Laboratory Operations and Critical Results
text: ### 2.2 Scope PRO-009 applies to **LAB-005, LAB-007, LAB-010, LAB-012, LAB-014 and LAB-024 only**. Other abnormal results (for example hemoglobin, creatinine, ferritin, NT-proBNP) are flagged in the report but not telephoned.

title: Laboratory Operations and Critical Results
text: ### 2.3 Critical values (LD-01) | Test | Critical value | |---|---| | Potassium (LAB-005) | **6.2 mmol/L or higher, or 2.9 mmol/L or lower** (FPA-01) | | hs-troponin (LAB-007) | **100 ng/L or higher** | | INR (LAB-010) | **5.0 or higher** | | Blood culture (LAB-012) | Any positive bottle | | Lactate (LAB-014) | **4.0 mmol/L or higher** | | C. difficile (LAB-024) | Any positive result; also notify Infection Control (PRO-012, HO-06) |

title: Laboratory Operations and Critical Results
text: ### 2.4 Time and method (FPA-13) 1. The result is verified in LabLink by laboratory staff. 2. The laboratory **telephones the responsible clinician within 20 minutes of verification** (not of collection). 3. The recipient reads back the patient name, identifiers, test, value and units; the laboratory records recipient, time, and read-back. 4. If the responsible clinician cannot be reached, the call goes to the covering clinician; from version 2, to the pager after two failed attempts. 5. A call outside 20 minutes is reported as a notification deviation and reviewed by the Laboratory Director and Quality (DEP-013).

title: Infection Prevention and Isolation Manual
text: ## 3. Isolation Categories | Category | Used for | Key measures | |---|---|---| | Standard | All patients | Hand hygiene, personal protective equipment by risk | | Contact | Resistant organisms, wounds with drainage | Gown and gloves; single room preferred | | **Contact-enteric** | **C. difficile infection (DIS-023)** | Gown and gloves; single room with dedicated toilet; **soap-and-water hand hygiene** (alcohol rub does not remove spores); dedicated equipment; sporicidal cleaning | | Droplet | Influenza-like and pneumococcal outbreaks | Surgical mask; single room | | Airborne | Open tuberculosis, measles | Negative-pressure room; respirator |

title: Infection Prevention and Isolation Manual
text: ## 4. C. difficile Precautions (FPA-10) 1. **Trigger:** a positive C. difficile result (LAB-024), or three or more unformed stools in 24 hours in a patient at risk, which allows precautions to start before the result. 2. **Start:** immediately on the call from the laboratory (version 2); the ward nurse records the start time. 3. **Duration:** precautions continue until **72 hours after diarrhea has resolved** (formed stool or return to baseline, FPA-10). Discharge or transfer before that time requires the receiving unit to be informed. 4. **Room and toilet:** single room with dedicated toilet or commode; no shared bathroom. 5. **Cleaning:** sporicidal agent daily and at terminal clean. 6. **Antibiotic review:** stewardship (HO-04) reviews the need for the inciting antibiotic. 7. **Treatment:** oral vancomycin 125 mg every 6 hours for 10 days (DG-05, MP-04).

title: Infection Prevention and Isolation Manual
text: ## 5. Outbreak Triggers Two or more hospital-onset C. difficile cases on the same ward within 7 days, or any cluster of three or more related infections, prompt notification of the Head of Infection Control, a ward review and enhanced cleaning. No outbreak was declared in the dataset.

section: 2. PRO-011: Discharge Planning and Follow-up Scheduling (version 2, effective 2025-06-01)
text: ## 2. PRO-011: Discharge Planning and Follow-up Scheduling (version 2, effective 2025-06-01)

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention
section: 2.1 Required elements before a patient leaves
text: ### 2.1 Required elements before a patient leaves 1. **Reconciled medication list** (PRO-001, HO-02), with changes explained and the patient given the list. 2. **Contact verification:** the patient's telephone number and an emergency contact are read back and confirmed (strengthened by PRO-016 version 2). 3. **Follow-up appointments booked** before discharge, with dates on the patient's summary. 4. **Pending results and tests** (for example INR) assigned to a named clinician. 5. **Warfarin patients: INR check within 72 hours of discharge** scheduled before departure (FPA-05; HO-04). 6. Equipment, diet and activity instructions; sick-day rules for patients on ACE inhibitors, mineralocorticoid antagonists, diuretics, metformin or SGLT2 inhibitors (DG-01, DG-02). 7. Discharge summary sent to the primary physician within 24 hours.

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention
text: ### 2.2 Documentation The discharge time is recorded to the minute because follow-up deadlines are counted from it.

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention
text: ## 3. PRO-016: Heart-Failure Post-Discharge Follow-up

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention
text: ### 3.1 Standard (FPA-06; all versions) For every patient discharged after an admission for heart failure, or with HFrEF (DIS-004) as an active problem: - **Telephone call within 48 hours of discharge** by Care Coordination. - **Clinic visit within 7 days of discharge** at the heart-failure clinic (DEP-003). - INR check within 72 hours if on warfarin (PRO-007).

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention

title: Discharge, Follow-up and Readmission Prevention
text: ### 4.1 MediCore Heart-Failure Readmission Risk Score (fictional) One point each: admission for heart failure in the past 12 months; eGFR below 45; NT-proBNP above the age-band threshold at discharge (DG-01); atrial fibrillation; living alone; unreliable telephone contact. A score of **3 or more** triggers a nurse home-visit offer. PAT-011 scored 3 at the first discharge (atrial fibrillation, NT-proBNP 4,820 pg/mL, prior recent admission), which did not trigger an outreach because the score field was not completed.
